articles.title: Amazon Starts Charging Significantly Above RRP for Nintendo Preorders in the UK
articles.summary: Amazon in the UK has started charging up to £70 more than other major retailers for several highly anticipated Nintendo preorders, such as Zelda's 40th Anniversary Switch 2 and Metroid Ravenous Special Edition.
articles.body:
Amazon is charging significantly more than the recommended retail price for several newly announced Nintendo products in the UK, with some preorders currently listed for up to £70 or more above the prices being charged by other major retailers.

The price differences have caught the attention of Nintendo fans following the back-to-back Nintendo Direct presentations, which revealed a host of new games and products, including the wildly popular The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary range and the long-awaited Ocarina of Time remake , alongside new Switch 2 games such as Metroid Ravenous .

The most striking example is the 40th Anniversary Zelda Switch 2 console . Nintendo's UK price was £434.99, while most other major retailers have listed the console at £429.99. Amazon, however, has been taking preorders at £499.99, making it £70 more expensive than the cheapest listings elsewhere.

Switch 2 - The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Edition

Switch 2 - Pro Controller The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Edition

Switch 2 Carrying Case The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Edition & Screen Protector

The same thing is happening with the other Zelda 40th Anniversary accessories. The special edition Switch 2 Pro Controller has an RRP of £79.99, but Amazon has it listed for £89.99. The matching carry case, meanwhile, is priced at £39.99 on Amazon compared to Nintendo's £29.99 RRP.

And it's not just the Zelda products. Amazon has also listed the Metroid Ravenous Special Edition at £119.99, despite the game's RRP being £99.99 and other major UK retailers listing it at that lower price.

The Special Edition has already proved particularly difficult to find, making the higher Amazon price even more notable for fans trying to secure a preorder. Yet, despite the increase in price, it still went on to sell out in record time.

Metroid Ravenous Special Edition preorders are live at Amazon Price: £119.99 Release Date: January 28, 2027 See here: #ad pic.twitter.com/2X6o7VCk89 — IGN UK Finds (@IGNUKDeals) September 11, 2026

Metroid Ravenous Special Edition preorders are live at Amazon Price: £119.99 Release Date: January 28, 2027 See here: #ad pic.twitter.com/2X6o7VCk89

The obvious answer is that Amazon is simply charging what it thinks people will pay.

That's speculation, to be clear, because Amazon hasn't explained why these Nintendo products are being listed above their RRP. But the pricing does raise the question of whether Amazon is pricing some of these highly sought-after products according to expected demand, rather than simply matching the recommended retail price used by Nintendo and other retailers.

We've seen something similar happen with the Pokémon TCG in the US , where extremely popular products can appear on Amazon at prices far above their MSRP when demand is high.

Notably, Amazon doesn't charge customers at the point they place a preorder for most physical products, with payment generally taken when the item is preparing to dispatch.

It's wishful thinking, but it means Amazon could still lower the price between now and release, potentially bringing these Nintendo products back in line with the RRP before customers are actually charged.

If you're feeling particularly charitable, you could speculate that with Nintendo's 40th Anniversary Zelda products and the Metroid Ravenous Special Edition proving difficult to find, perhaps the higher prices are an attempt to discourage scalpers and opportunistic bulk buying.

If that is the intention, though, it doesn't appear to have worked particularly well. The products are still selling out almost instantly, and anyone willing to pay the inflated price can simply place their preorder and hope that Amazon's price drops before release.

Amazon is charging £70 more than most other UK retailers for preorders of the Zelda 40th Anniversary Switch 2. Nintendo's own store was charging £434.99, while most other retailers settled at £429.99. Amazon? £499.99! 👉 #ad pic.twitter.com/XBpRK5tgtT — IGN UK Finds (@IGNUKDeals) September 10, 2026

Amazon is charging £70 more than most other UK retailers for preorders of the Zelda 40th Anniversary Switch 2. Nintendo's own store was charging £434.99, while most other retailers settled at £429.99. Amazon? £499.99! 👉 #ad pic.twitter.com/XBpRK5tgtT

The less charitable interpretation is simply that Amazon knows these are products Nintendo fans desperately want, and has decided that there's money to be made from that demand.

But, for now, we don't know which explanation is correct.

What we do know is that Amazon's prices are currently well above Nintendo's recommended prices, while other major UK retailers are offering the same products for considerably less.

IGN has contacted Amazon for clarification and comment on the pricing and will update this story if the retailer provides an explanation.

You can usually find Robert lost in open-world RPG games like Elden Ring and Cyberpunk 2077. Outside of gaming, his passions include reading comics (especially Superman, Batman, and Spider-Man), taking photos, and keeping up with the latest in film and TV.

His primary coverage focuses on tracking down the best gaming deals and diving into the fast-paced world of Trading Card Games (TCGs). He regularly covers everything from the latest releases in Pokémon TCG and the most expensive cards to comprehensive Magic: The Gathering buying guides . As a massive Doctor Who fan, he also keeps a close eye on physical media deals like Doctor Who Blu-ray preorders , and occasionally steps away from commerce to contribute reviews for the site, such as his review of Doctor Who's latest season .

articles.title: Paul Greengrass Explains The Uprising's Robin Hood Ending
articles.summary: Director Paul Greengrass breaks down the ending of The Uprising, explaining its connection to the legend of Robin Hood, key plot twists, and character fates.
articles.body:
Director Paul Greengrass’ The Uprising chronicles the Peasants’ Revolt of 1381 , but uses this actual historical event as a set-up for what had secretly been a Robin Hood origin movie until a recent trailer revealed the truth. (Nowhere in the film, though, is Andrew Garfield’s protagonist referred to as Robin Hood. His peasant farmer character is known simply as Ploughman.)

After the Peasants’ Revolt is crushed by King Richard II (Woody Norman), the Ploughman, along with other survivors like Alyce (Thomasin McKenzie), abandon their previous lives and take to the woods to become outlaws. In the film’s closing moments, Ploughman and his highwaymen, camouflaged in earthy-hued clothing, emerge from the forest to attack the King’s convoy.

The Uprising’s Robin Hood Ending Explained by Director Paul Greengrass

After his fellow outlaws kill the King’s guards and he personally slays the Mayor of London (Jonny Lee Miller) in one-on-one combat, the Ploughman – or, Robin Hood if you will – pins the King to the ground. But rather than kill him, he leaves the monarch with a warning: we will haunt you forever.

The final shot of the movie is of Windsor Castle where we can hear the King screaming from night terrors. During the first half of the movie, Richard II had been paralyzed with fear and indecision, praying to God to save him from those he dreams are coming to get him. Richard II eventually finds his backbone as a leader, proclaiming he will grant the rebelling peasants’ petitions for freedoms. But then at Smithfield on June 15, 1381, Richard II betrays the serfs, and has his troops kill a slew of them, including rebel leaders Wat Tyler (Cosmo Jarvis) and John Ball (Jamie Bell). In real life, Tyler was killed there and authorities hunted down a great number of rebels in the following weeks.

Ploughman and Alyce are among those rebels who escape Smithfield alive, making their way back to Ploughman’s farm where he finds his home burned down. With nothing left, Ploughman weeps at the graves of his dead family and takes fistfuls of dirt and smears it across his face. The Ploughman is symbolically buried with them, and the outlaw who will inspire the legend of Robin Hood is born. The film then jumps ahead a year to depict the attack on the King’s convoy described above.

I recently chatted with the film’s writer-director, Paul Greengrass, who explained that his intent was always to incorporate the legend of Robin Hood into his story and that he was supportive of Focus Features’ brief pivot to marketing the film as The Uprising: The Rise of Robin Hood.

IGN: Focus very briefly marketed The Uprising as literally The Rise of Robin Hood. What were your thoughts on that? And is that true to your film?

Paul Greengrass: I believe entirely so. So let me explain that because completely is the answer, 100%. I'll tell you why. So I sit down on Day Two of the [Covid-19] pandemic to write this film that's going to be about a fictional farmer because I knew that I was going to do that in a part of the world that I knew, those Essex-Suffolk marshes. It's where the Greengrasses come from, but a little bit north of there, but essentially that world. And I grew up in Gravesend in Kent, which is very close to Maidstone where he goes. That's all very, very familiar to me and I understood all that world.

I'm going to tell the story of this fictional character. So what I need to do is have him be there at the start of the uprising in this tax collection scene, and then I'm going to have to have him join the Kent rebels, and then he's going to march to London, take part in the revolution or the uprising, see the dreams and hopes of the revolution or the uprising betrayed by the revolution itself, and then ultimately by the king, because the history books tell us that the rebellion, the uprising, was crushed.

Okay. If you're making my movie, I can't end with, "And then Ploughman dies," because I don't want to make that movie. That's not a movie. That's not a historical epic. He's got to survive, right? That's point one. Because you want the dreams of The Uprising to live on. So he escapes, he goes to the forest, and he's reborn as an outlaw. That always made perfect sense to me.

IGN: And historically it rings true too.

Paul Greengrass: Completely. And let me tell you why in two really profound ways. First of all, and I knew this obviously before I started writing the film, because I was charting it out in my mind in those early days of lockdown because you start with, "Okay, the hero's journey. Okay, simple farmer. He's going to do that. And I don't want him to die, so he's going to have to take the idea, as you say, and live on." And he's going to go there, and he's going to become an outlaw. Okay.

I knew by then that the first reference to Robin Hood was a few years before the Peasants' Revolt in the poem, Piers Plowman . What he's referring to in the poem is Rober Hood or Rob the Hood or whatever, that was basically a moniker given to a criminal or an outlaw. And there was clearly stories passing around. You're not talking courtly poets. You're talking about down where its history is not really recorded.

You get little glimpses of it, and that's one in Piers Plowman, that people told stories about an outlaw called Rob or Rob the Hood. That's the very first reference, just literally a few years before the Peasants' Revolt. And other characters in the Peasants' Revolt are referenced in the poem, like Tom Hollander's character [who gets] his head chopped off. He's referencing it because it's really the dream of a farmer. That's why I called my farmer Ploughman as a nod to that poem.

Only I know that and other people who did English [as a] major, but it made sense to me. After the uprising was crushed – now, we're talking history, not movie – after the uprising was crushed, what changed? The truth is subterraneanly, a huge amount changed because people started to feel differently about themselves. This was the first moment that people, ordinary folk, ordinary men and women, came center stage and said, "We matter. What we want matters. Our rights matter." It's the first moment. And from then on, the crown, the oligarchs could never quite take the people for granted. You can see that echoing down the next 100, 200 years.

IGN: You can almost draw a line from that to later rebellions in Ireland and the United States.

Paul Greengrass: Sure, the United States. Because what emerged out of the Peasants' Revolt, not the next day, but over time, this sense that individual rights lead to individual representations was the seed that was planted, that flowered. It flowered ultimately in the Enlightenment. It flowered in the American Revolution, which was about getting rid of the king and ruling ourselves alone. And there's a very famous work of history by a woman called Barbara Tuchman called A Distant Mirror. It's a study of the 14th century, and the Peasants' Revolt was a big part of it. And she basically makes the argument in the book that you draw this line from the disturbances of the 14th century all the way through the Enlightenment up through the American Constitution. It's part of the journey towards individual representation.

So the thrust of it, to have an ending where my character says we're going to rule ourselves alone was absolutely emotionally true, true to the movie, but also interestingly with the thrust of where the world went. But the second more interesting point for your question is that the legend of Robin Hood, the real explosion of the popularity of outlaw stories, is all after the Peasants' Revolt. That's when various outlaw stories started to be really wildly popular. And the most popular of course of all is Robin Hood. And why is that? Because it was a way people kept those dreams alive.

There was nobody ever called Robin Hood. He was a superhero, really. He was a guy they told stories about who stood up against the powerful when they felt powerless. And so they kept the dream alive, and he became popular. A bit like in the '30s, people told stories about outlaws like Bonnie and Clyde. It's kind of what happens in hard times. And that Robin Hood was a yeoman. He was an outlaw. He was a bit like our guy. And I'm not saying he was in the Peasants' Revolt, but he emerges after in that sensibility. The Robin of Loxley Robin Hood, the disaffected, the dispossessed aristocrat, that's a Victorian 20th century invention of the Robin Hood myth because it's highly romantic.

And what actually happened was, of course, when they're going to bring a movie out, they do marketing screenings, and this all came up in the marketing and an American audience didn't know it, that this is where the legend of Robin Hood came from. And it was like something that in these screenings, particularly young people by the way, "Oh, that's really cool. We didn't know that." So that's where it all came from. So you go, "Okay, well, let's push a bit of that into social media." That made sense to me. I have no problem with it. It's true to the movie and true to where that legend came from.

IGN: As I watched the film, I knew enough about that era and that particular moment in English history to be like, "Oh, it's not like Andrew Garfield pulls out a knife and goes, ‘The name's Hood, Robin Hood.’ But I'm like, "Oh, I see. He's setting up this is where those outlaws come from."

Paul Greengrass: He's no longer Ploughman. When he puts some earth on his face, takes his family with him, takes the land that he's lived on. And now, he's reborn. He's reborn with a hood and a mask. He's going to be an outlaw forever. And then you enter a sort of cinematic place where, "Fuck it. I'm going to ambush the king," because you want to symbolize that he lives on, and that I think is really cool and satisfying.

And you've got to have a movie that entertains people. When I wrote that original screenplay, do you know what the title was? The Hood. That's what I called it six years ago. It was always called The Hood. Then it got retitled. By the way, I was happy to call it The Uprising. I called it The Hood, then I called it The Rage, and then I called it The Uprising.

IGN: Think about Braveheart. You can't end it with William Wallace just getting disemboweled. You have to have the sword flying into the field. You got to know that it was worth something. Even Spartacus, when he dies, the whole “I'm Spartacus!”, all of that, even it's trying to find that silver lining within the real history. You can't change history, but you can modulate it to have a meaning.

Paul Greengrass: You said it, you keep the dream – the flame of freedom stays alive, and the hero's journey continues. And I never wanted my character to die because it didn't feel interesting to me. It felt interesting to me to end him as an outlaw. That was the place where he was headed, and a sort of mythic one where he shed all his identity, became a sort of mythic, a never named outlaw who took on the king and said, "No, I could kill you, but instead, we'll just stay and haunt you forever."

The Most Famous Movie and TV Characters Who've Met Robin Hood

IGN: Obviously, there was at least a little back and forth between the UK exhibitor and the US in terms of the Robin Hood subtitle. Do you think it's because you mentioned the test audiences here in the States and the younger people not knowing, is it something that maybe UK audiences just know? Or is there something more about the fact that we've had all these Robin Hood movies lately?

Paul Greengrass: Honestly and truly, I think all of this is sort of beside the point. First of all, let's take the Focus thing. So they're trying to do a campaign for the movie, which is their job, and I think they're doing a great job. I love the trailer. I love all their materials. What's interesting to me is, it's always interesting when you release a film, you see how sophisticated and different selling movies is. It's hard. It's hard. And how important it is, we're never going to keep cinema alive unless we find a way of connecting with audiences.

In the old days, like when you made a Bourne movie 25 years ago, whatever it was, 20 years ago, you build it and then you pump it out with a thousand TV ads. It was like mass mainstream marketing, but that's not how movies are sold now, and particularly not a Focus movie, which is what this is. You've got to connect with audiences much more directly through social media and all the rest of it . So there are hundreds of these messages of which some contained that Robin Hood thing. I was good with it.

In terms of the UK distributor, it was like one story because they phoned the guy, and he didn't happen to have known at that point what the next phase [was] and it's like suddenly it becomes a story and you go, "Oh my God, is that really what..." As if he said he didn't like the film. He loves the film. He's releasing it for God's sake. He'll be trying to find his way in the UK of reaching the audience that will want to come and see this movie. I don't know because I have nothing to do with marketing, but I suspect it feels to me logically, what they tried to do is find where their audience is and then try and ease it out. And what's the next adjacent bit that you can get? Oh, cool. That audience might be interested in a bit of Robin Hood. Well, it's in the movie. So we'll try and target that. That will make sense to me. The other guy, his date is later. We're not releasing in the UK until the 9th of October. So he's got slightly different issues. He doesn't want to go too early because you want, as I understand it, to unfold your marketing campaign by degrees. You don't want to come out and tell everybody what the ending is first.

IGN: I was a little surprised about the Robin Hood trailer reveal, because to me, I was treating that as a spoiler. That's the end of the movie. And I was a little shocked at them putting that out there, to be honest.

Paul Greengrass: What they felt, I'm sure, is that it will tell people what's in the movie in a good way, in a way that will make a younger male audience want to come and explore it, because [otherwise they might think] it's not a Robin Hood movie.

The Uprising is now playing in North American theaters.

Editor’s note: This interview has been edited for clarity.

articles.title: Hamilton ‘regaña’ a Bellingham por no tener carnet: “Pareces mi madre”
articles.standfirst: Las dos estrellas británicas comparten protagonismo en el estreno de la actualización de un videojuego
articles.summary: Las dos estrellas británicas comparten protagonismo en el estreno de la actualización de un videojuego
articles.body: El Gran Premio de España de Fórmula 1 en Madring nos está dejando escenas de todo tipo: presentaciones de coches en plena Plaza de Las Ventas, pilotos visitando el Santiago Bernabéu... y crossovers inesperados para estrenar videojuegos, como la actualización del F1 25 de EA Sports que se ha lanzado coincidiendo con la carrerra española. EA Sports ha reunido nada más y nada menos que a dos estrellas como Lewis Hamilton y Jude Bellingham para protagonizar el vídeo de presentación de las novedades del juego. Aprovechando que ambos están en Madrid por sus compromisos deportivos (Bellingham juega contra el Rayo mañana y el heptacampeón está descubriendo Madring este fin de semana) se han juntado para desafiarse con los monoplazas virtuales. El mejor momento llega cuando Hamilton le pregunta a su compatriota si sabe conducir... en la vida real y Bellingham le confiesa su realidad al respecto. De hecho, uno de los rasgos más pecualiares del 5 blanco es precisamente ese, que acude a los entrenamientos y a los partidos siempre como pasajero porque... no conduce. Cuando se 'entera', el siete veces campeón del mundo se escandaliza "¿Pero no tienes carnet de conducir?" "No, ni carnet ni nada...", confiesa. "¿Cómo? ¡Pero si tienes 23 años!", se pregunta confundido el piloto de Ferrari... y a Bellingham no le queda más remedio que reconocerlo: "Sí, está mal.. Lo sé, lo sé. Todo el mundo me dice lo mismo: ¡pareces mi madre!". A lo que Lewis responde con una sonora carcajada final... Sin duda, un simpático vídeo... en el que especialmente Hamilton demuestra sus grandes dotes de actor. La actualización del EA Sports F1 25: 2026 Season Edition incorpora nuevos pilotos y equipos de F2, cambios en los monoplazas de 2026 (por ejemplo, los alerones Macarena) y diferentes diseños especiales de los que han lucido los coches en Grandes Premios de este temporada. Además, viene con un fin de semana de juego gratuito en Xbox y PC. Los nuevos jugadores podrán conseguir F1 25: 2026 Season Edition con un 30 % de descuento hasta el 14 de septiembre, mientras que quienes ya tengan F1 25 podrán adquirir el 2026 Season Pack con un 20 % de descuento en todas las plataformas compatibles.

articles.title: GTA 6 Developer Rockstar Says It Was Forced to Put Privacy Films on Its Buildings After Drones Were Used to Snap Photos Through Office Windows
articles.summary: Rockstar Games has released its opening note in the employment tribunal to determine the fate of the 31 GTA 6 developers it fired last year, and in doing so has revealed the extreme lengths it goes to in order to prevent security breaches.
articles.body:
Rockstar Games has released its opening note in the employment tribunal to determine the fate of the 31 GTA 6 developers it fired last year, and in doing so has revealed the extreme lengths it goes to in order to prevent security breaches.

The hearing, which got underway yesterday at Glasgow Employment Tribunal , revolves around allegations made by the Independent Workers of Great Britain union (IWGB) — allegations Rockstar strongly denies. The IWGB claims the staff were unlawfully blacklisted and targeted for their union activities, and that the manner in which they were dismissed was also unlawful because it came without disciplinary process or right of appeal.

Rockstar has insisted it fired the staff because they leaked GTA 6 game features via Discord, not because they were trying to unionize. 34 members of staff at Rockstar were dismissed — 31 in the UK and three in Canada — sparking protests outside the office of Rockstar North in Edinburgh, Scotland, and parent company Take-Two in London.

Rockstar North and Take-Two Office Protest Photos Nov 2025

Rockstar maintains that at the time of the dismissals it didn’t know that the people it fired were involved with a union. As for the Discord comments at the heart of this case, Rockstar says they had to do with GTA 6 features, overall progress and timelines to launch, as well as company IT security protocols. Rockstar believes that if the Discord comments had leaked they would have been big gaming news and might even have affected Take-Two’s share price. When Rockstar officially announced that GTA 6 would be delayed by six months to November 19, 2026, the market value of Take-Two plummeted $3.75 billion in a single day.

In its note, Rockstar goes into detail on the intense scrutiny it is under as developer of GTA 6 — predicted to be the biggest entertainment launch of all time — and how it works to prevent security breaches.

“Guarding the secrets of the unique gameplay and design are akin to Apple protecting the iPhone or Coke protecting its formula,” Rockstar said, adding that it adopts “the security posture of a Wall Street bank.”

Rockstar’s secrecy is well-known within the industry, as are the security breaches it has faced in the past. Last month it suffered one of the most high-profile video game leaks in history when GTA 6 gameplay was published online ahead of the game’s Netflix gameplay reveal. But that was just the latest in a string of leaks that have affected GTA 6 over its decade-long development.

In April 2025, Rockstar dismissed an employee in Lincoln, UK, who it alleged disclosed confidential information about GTA 6 to a third party who then published the information to social media. Rockstar dismissed an employee in the U.S. in November 2023 and another in India in November 2025 for two separate acts of information leaking.

“The standards and expectations regarding information security and privacy are exponentially beyond that of most employers,” Rockstar continued in its opening note. It said all visitors to Rockstar’s offices must sign non-disclosure agreements, and any contractors working on site are escorted, while there, by security. Remote working for employees is severely restricted. Flash drives / USB keys and other external storage devices are banned. Photography at work is strictly forbidden. Employees’ personal laptops, tablets and phones are blocked from connecting to the Rockstar systems. Rockstar staff are ordered not to disclose confidential information even to family members.

“The Respondent’s [Rockstar's] detailed Social Media Guidelines confirm that even innocuous pictures of an employee’s desk could unacceptably reveal confidential information,” Rockstar said. The company faces regular attacks on its security and systems, and was forced to put privacy films on its buildings after drones were used to try and photograph through office windows. Staff have been harassed online, Rockstar said. Rockstar employs a full-time team of five investigators and a director to monitor for and investigate potential data leaks. Its employees face phishing and social engineering attacks seeking to trick them into giving up passwords and login credentials.

“Some of those attacks have been successful,” Rockstar said, including a 2022 leak of dozens of videos of unfinished development footage of GTA 6. That was obtained through phishing, which gave a hacker access to an employee’s computer and from there, material shared on Rockstar’s own internal Slack communication channels.

“The history of leaks has made the Respondent hypervigilant to lock information down as tightly as possible,” Rockstar added. “Most recently, in the last few weeks, a hacking group attempted to blackmail the Respondent,” Rockstar said, referencing the CyberLeek breach. “If any more proof was needed that the Respondent’s sensitivity to security and confidentiality is justified, it is the wiping of $2 billion from the Respondent’s parent company’s share value within a few days as that recent hack became public.”

“The Claimants were all aware of this culture, referencing it numerous times on their own Discord posts,” Rockstar said.

Even More GTA 6 Screenshots from Rockstar Games

Rockstar’s note goes on to discuss the extreme levels of scrutiny it is subject to, pointing out the frequency of coffee shop trips by employees and pizza deliveries to the Rockstar offices have been monitored by fans, and traffic volumes by its workplaces were allegedly tracked in a bid to get an inside track on the GTA 6 release date.

It also noted how in 2025 two innocuous tweets from employees sparked a (mistaken) fan theory that a new GTA 6 trailer would be released on December 27, 2025 as a precursor to sales of the game itself. “The theory snowballed from the backwaters of the internet to industry and mainstream coverage around the globe,” Rockstar said.

The hearing runs until October 16, a month before GTA 6 comes out. The workers want reinstatement or, failing that, compensation, as well as a finding from the tribunal that their dismissals were unfair. The IWGB alleges that on the day of the dismissals, employees were called into meetings, told they were being fired with immediate effect and escorted from the building. Workers who were not at the office allege they were informed during phone calls lasting around two minutes before being locked out of their work accounts. The IWGB also alleges that one of the dismissed workers, Will Mesilane, had to leave the UK and return to Australia after Rockstar withdrew his work visa and reported him to the Home Office, without giving him a chance to appeal.

In a statement issued to IGN, a spokesperson for Rockstar Games insisted the studio was ready to defend itself from the claims. The statement is below:

“Rockstar Games' position has been clear and consistent throughout. Individuals across the UK and Canada were dismissed for gross misconduct following the sharing of confidential company information, not because of alleged trade union membership or activity. We reject the claims and will defend them vigorously before the tribunal.”

Jason Lewis, former Rockstar employee and IWGB Union member, commented: “For almost a year, the truth about what happened to us has been buried by Rockstar and surrounded by speculation. Now we finally get the chance to put it on the record. None of us imagined that talking to each other about our working conditions would turn our lives upside down and catapult us into the centre of a global media storm. As the world prepares for the release of GTA 6, we are reliving the heartbreak of being thrown out of a project we poured so much of our lives into. We lost our jobs, our income, our community and the chance to see the game through to release after spending years helping to build it. It was devastating.

“We have fought tooth and nail to get to this point, not just to be able to win justice for ourselves, but to draw a line in the sand for any employer that thinks it can attack workers for unionising. It has been an emotional journey and it is not over yet, but we can now see the finish line, and justice at last feels within reach.”

Last month, the fired Rockstar workers told fans they shouldn’t boycott GTA 6 to protest on their behalf , but buy T-shirts launched to raise money towards their legal costs instead. Alex Marshall, president of the IWGB, said: “We believe Rockstar has tried to get away with Grand Theft Employment Rights. After a year of fighting to get answers, we hope this tribunal will finally back them into a corner and bring the truth to light. As the world gets its first proper look at GTA 6, this hearing will give people a chance to look behind the scenes at what happened to the workers who helped make it.

“That is why this hearing matters for every worker across the UK, whether their job is in entertainment, education or anywhere else. It is a moment to send a clear message to each of them: you have the right to join a union, that right is protected by law, and employers cannot punish you for exercising it.

“If Rockstar can get away with firing workers for organising, then every employer in Britain gets the message that they can do the same. We cannot let that happen.”

Meanwhile, negotiations are ongoing between Rockstar and the IWGB over formal union recognition, even amid this legal battle. The union wants greater pay transparency, protection from post-release layoffs, an end to "crunch," and improved flexible working arrangements, it’s said. If an agreement is reached, Rockstar would become the biggest recognised unionised game studio in the UK. Workers hope to secure recognition before the release of GTA 6.

articles.title: Fans Are Reportedly Getting $20 Off Ocarina of Time Preorders With a Hidden Coupon at Walmart
articles.summary: Walmart shoppers are supposedly using a hidden promo code to knock $20 off The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time preorders, bringing it down from $70 to $50, but it might not work for everyone.
articles.body:
Fans are potentially saving as much as $20 on their preorder of the highly anticipated The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake for Nintendo Switch 2 .

The game is already $10 off at Walmart and Amazon , but we've now seen multiple reports of shoppers getting another $10 knocked off at Walmart by using a specific promo code.

That code is SAVE3X , and we decided to put it to the test ourselves. Fellow Senior Commerce Editor Chris Reed successfully preordered the game with the code, bringing his total down to just $49.88. Unfortunately, our Senior Social Producer Seth Macy wasn't so lucky when he tried it himself. Womp womp.

So, this is very much a YMMV situation, but it's certainly worth trying if you're planning to pick up the remake anyway, especially if you want that rather lovely limited-edition "textured foil" cover art.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (Switch 2)

There does seem to be another quirk to the promotion, too. From the reports I've seen , shoppers who have successfully applied the code are selecting " delivery" or "pickup" rather than the standard " shipping" option at checkout.

I've also been told that SAVE3X is supposedly a Walmart 'new customer code' and works only on the first three online purchases you make at the retailer as a new customer. But, once again, IGN's Chris Reed was able to use the code and has shopped at Walmart plenty of times before. So, who knows!

But even after all that, if the coupon code still doesn't work for you, getting a physical copy for $10 below MSRP isn't exactly a bad consolation prize either.

Well, it's actually pretty straightforward. As has become Nintendo's custom with this console generation , the game's MSRP is $59.99 for digital and $69.99 for physical copies.

That said, Amazon and Walmart have been pretty consistent about undercutting that $69.99 physical price, often bringing games down to match, or even beat, the $59.99 digital price. It's a neat little incentive to buy physical, particularly if you're already planning to preorder.

We've seen the same thing with other Switch 2 exclusives, including Star Fox , Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave , and Switch Sports Resort , among others. Just bear in mind that these lower prices are generally a preorder perk, with the price going back up once the game actually launches.

And, if you're opting for a physical copy, there's another nice bonus here: Ocarina of Time comes entirely on the cartridge. There's no game key card nonsense to worry about.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake launches for Switch 2, November 5, 2026. As you can tell, preorders are now live, and have been incredibly popular so far.

articles.title: PlayStation’s Future Has Never Looked Bleaker
articles.summary: Cutting ties with Kojima and poor Wolverine reviews are just the latest issues in a difficult generation for PlayStation. The platform's future has never looked bleaker.
articles.body:
This is an IGN opinion piece from Matt Purslow, who has been there from day one for every PlayStation generation since the PS2. He loves the style of narrative single-player adventures that Sony's studios have historically championed.

It’s impossible to know how PlayStation bosses felt after seeing many critics walk away from Insomniac’s Wolverine with an apathetic shrug . A sub-80 on Metacritic is infamously considered a disaster in the triple-A space, and so Sony certainly won’t be thrilled, but it would be easy for the company to brush this away as an uncharacteristic miss. Even Capcom, across its near decade-long hot streak , put out the middling Exoprimal, after all. However, that would require wilfully ignoring the sad reality that PlayStation Studios is currently far from fertile ground for single-player adventures.

What was once the miracle recipe behind Uncharted has now become the de facto template for almost every Sony project, resulting in an incredibly polished homogeneous mass. It’s a video game design rulebook later refined by the likes of The Last of Us and God of War: lavish cutscenes, approachable combat with a light sprinkling of RPG skills, sneaking through waist-high grass to perform simple stealth takedowns, and filling a rage meter to trigger an ultimate ability. Ten years ago, this was all incredibly exciting. Five years ago, it was comfortingly familiar. Today, it’s wearing thin. Never has it been clearer that PlayStation Studios needs to find the next evolutionary stage of the “traditional” video game. Never has it been clearer that it needs its next Metal Gear Solid, the revolutionary Hideo Kojima game that defined what we could expect from PlayStation back in 1998.

Now would be a very good time, then, for Sony to cancel Hideo Kojima’s PlayStation-exclusive spiritual successor to Metal Gear Solid.

“In mid-June of this year, we unexpectedly received notice from PlayStation Studios that they would cancel the Physint project,” explained Kojima in a recent social media post . The project is now, in a bizarre twist of fate, being financed by PlayStation’s direct competitor, Xbox. That itself is a whole cursed kettle of fish – it’s no doubt a kick in the teeth for the recently disbanded stealth specialists at Arkane to see Microsoft invest untold millions in a Kojima espionage game – but when it comes to PlayStation, the brand has cut ties with a distinctive creative powerhouse at a time when it’s in desperate need of a distinctive creative direction.

First announced during a Sony State of Play in early 2024 , Physint was described as “a completely new 'Action Espionage' for the next-generation.” That specific wording, of course, is intended to evoke Metal Gear Solid, which sports the tagline “Tactical Espionage Action” across each of the series’ logos. The intention was crystal clear: Sony and Kojima were working together on a successor to MGS, and PlayStation would be the place to play it.

There are several obvious reasons why a new Metal Gear Solid in all but name would be good for PlayStation (and now stands to be good for Xbox). The name “Kojima” is pretty much as important as the MGS brand itself, and so a new Kojima game is potentially good business. The team at Kojima Productions are talented creatives, and so Physint has a high chance of being a critical success. And, perhaps most important, culturally speaking, Kojima’s “walking simulator” Death Stranding series has proved divisive, and so PlayStation Xbox gets to be the stage for his glorious return to the genre he’s so beloved for.

But there was more to this union than cultural “victories” and brand recognition. PlayStation has never felt more stagnant. The PS5 has been something of a disaster generation for Sony, and while there are numerous terrible business decisions to talk of – from Concord to physical media to pay-extra-to-stand-your-console-vertically – I believe one of the most crucial problems is that the PlayStation identity has begun to crumble. Historically, PlayStation has been the place to play exceptional, elite-tier single-player games that were constantly on the cutting edge of the medium. It’s a near-30-year reputation that goes right back to 1998’s Metal Gear Solid. But since the PS5 arrived in 2020, it’s been near-impossible to find the brand’s historic innovation in cinematic adventures. Somewhat ironically, Kojima’s own Death Stranding 2 is the alarming outlier.

Four of this generation’s major first-party exclusives – Ghost of Yotei, Marvel’s Spider-Man 2, God of War Ragnarok, and Horizon Forbidden West – are almost indistinguishable from their PS4 predecessors when it comes to how they play. Never mind the fact that there is significant overlap between each game’s design language; there’s a real sense that this generation has done little to advance the art form that so many buy a PlayStation for. The age of the glittering PlayStation exclusive – the “genre” that helped elevate the PS3 out of arrogant mediocrity and define the PS4 – feels well and truly over.

There was no guarantee, of course, that Physint could have been the miracle cure to reverse the rot. But if there was any project that could have reignited PlayStation’s spark, a spiritual successor to Metal Gear Solid directed by the man who started it all is the one I’d have put money on. Kojima is famously bold – his bizarre meta experiments in the early MGS games are the stuff of legend, and there’s no arguing against the fact that Death Stranding was an exercise in wild creativity, even if a big walk wasn’t your idea of a good time. If anyone was to be the spearhead for a new generation of PlayStation single-player, it was undoubtedly Kojima.

Just as important, though, is the nostalgia and trust in Metal Gear Solid. While Physint will surely (hopefully) build atop MGS’s achievements with creative new ideas, the fact that it’s an “Action Espionage” game provides it with just enough franchise energy that it’s not as risky as betting on a completely original idea. Physint is a much safer bet than Death Stranding ever was (even if connoisseurs know that the gulf between Death Stranding and MGS 5 is about as wide as a pencil).

In this way, Physint potentially could resemble the recently released The Blood of Dawnwalker, an RPG developed by The Witcher 3 developers which plays a lot like The Witcher 3, but features an innovative time pressure system that puts a new spin on choice and consequence. It sold over a million copies in just two days . In parallel, we saw Capcom’s Onimusha: Way of the Sword – a game that similarly blended a familiar base with fresh new ideas – also sell a million copies in 24 hours . It’s clear that people are hungry for something new, but that it’s easier to secure a sale if there’s some kind of connection to a prior experience. Physint could have been that for PlayStation. Now, it’s the project that could help define Xbox’s Project Helix generation.

Of course, a million copies in a day or two could well be considered small fry by PlayStation. It’s never been more apparent that money is the driving force behind Sony’s gaming division, and Kojima’s recent financial results could have poisoned the well. Dr. Serkan Toto, CEO of Japanese consultancy firm Kantan Games, recently said that Sony’s choice to pull out of its deal with Kojima Productions may well be due to the “steep” sales drop-off between Death Stranding and its 2025 sequel. Recent figures from Alinea Analytics suggest Death Stranding 2 has sold just 2.5 million copies – an understandable decline, considering a sequel to a divisive game about delivering packages across dangerous terrain was naturally going to be niche at best, but not the ideal outcome for a project that cost millions and took half a decade to make. Physint’s budget would likely eclipse Death Stranding 2’s, considering Kojima’s estimate in 2025 was that the game was still 5-6 years from completion, and its promised ambition no doubt demands increased investment. It’s the kind of situation that repels the spreadsheet suits at a corporation like Sony.

But the big picture question remains: if Kojima returning to the espionage genre that helped define PlayStation in the first place isn’t the correct move, then what is? If Sony doesn’t want to invest in arguably one of the most obvious solutions to push its signature single-player games forward and break its creative stalemate, then what will define the PlayStation 6? Sony’s own actions would suggest live-service – the company has continually attempted to break into the market and establish its own never-ending multiplayer game that can print money for a decade. And yet, despite millions invested, it has almost nothing to show for it. Concord is dead . The Last of Us Online cancelled . Destiny 2 wrapped up . Horizon Hunters Gathering sent back to the drawing board . No one’s playing Marathon, and even Sony’s one live-service victory, Helldivers 2, can’t command the attention it once did. It’s hard to see a good reason to buy a PlayStation 6, because it’s hard to see what PlayStation even means anymore.

Sony, of course, is about to bathe in what will surely be the biggest river of money in its lifetime thanks to Grand Theft Auto 6. Its exclusive marketing deal with Rockstar has done a phenomenal job of making it appear that GTA 6 is a PS5 exclusive to the casual eye, and so the biggest game of all time will no doubt bankroll PlayStation into the future. But GTA 6 only reinforces the question of PlayStation’s identity; right now, GTA's next online iteration is merely an assumption, and so the untold millions of copies sold on November 19 will have been bought to access a single-player video game. The constant survival of solo play despite decades of naysayers claiming multiplayer would wipe it out is something that can’t be ignored, and has there ever been a better home for single-player adventures than PlayStation? It’s an identity Sony would be foolish to squander.

Physint wasn’t necessarily the answer to PlayStation’s woes. Perhaps, if recent reports regarding Kojima’s approach to budget and deadlines are to be believed, it would only have caused more problems. But the question of PlayStation’s identity still needs an answer, and so, as Kojima departs for Xbox and Sony bosses continue to chase the live-service dragon, there’s never been more pressure on Naughty Dog. It feels like Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet has to be an Uncharted-like revolution that propels PlayStation single-player into a brave new future. Because if it relies on lavish cutscenes, approachable combat with a light sprinkling of RPG skills, sneaking through waist-high grass to perform simple stealth takedowns, and a rage meter that triggers an ultimate ability, it’s game over.

Matt Purslow is IGN's Executive Editor of Features.

articles.title: 'They Thought It Was Too Funny': Zach Cregger Says He's Cut Most of the Jokes From His Resident Evil Movie, Following Test Screenings
articles.summary: Resident Evil director Zach Cregger says he's cut most of movie's jokes, after test audiences apparently found the film "too funny."
articles.body:
Resident Evi l director Zach Cregger says he's cut most of movie's jokes, after test audiences apparently found the film "too funny."

Capcom loves including the occasional quip or witty one-liner in its Resident Evil game series — typically something cheesy from Leon S. Kennedy about going to bingo — so it's not surprising that Cregger also planned to include humor in his adaptation.

Cregger himself is known for mixing horror and dark humor to great effect, as seen in his previous projects Weapons and Barbarians. But you can also have too much of a good thing, the director has said.

"I learned that people really liked the movie, but they thought it was too funny," Cregger said of the film's test screenings, in an interview with The Hollywood Reporter . "So over the course of my testing, I stripped out as much of the jokes as possible.

"I then found that not only did the audience enjoy the movie more, but I also liked the movie a lot more," he continued. "A little bit of humor goes a long way in a horror movie, and there's not a single joke I took out of this movie that I miss."

Ahead of Resident Evil's arrival in theaters next week, Cregger has been busy discussing his process making the film, and also dealing with fan expectations. The director has said that he feels like he's been on something of an "apology tour" after having to explain some of his decisions, particularly around his choice to focus on an original character and story. Indeed, Cregger has even suggested that this will now be the only franchise he ever tries to adapt — though after promising signs of how the film will perform, has not ruled out working on a sequel .

In the meantime, Resident Evil releases on September 18 — just don't expect too many jokes.

articles.title: The Long Game: 4 Tactics to Master Early in Star Wars Zero Company
articles.body:
We’re back for another installment of our The Long Game series, where we focus on things you can invest in early in games that will pay off in the long run. Today we’re diving into Star Wars Zero Company, the turn-based tactics game from Bit Reactor that drops you into the twilight of the Clone Wars.

Zero Company gives you lots of ways to customize your team, including a variety of specializations (aka character classes), different weapon types, weapon mods, and equippable items that can define each character’s playstyle. You can swap all of these things at the Den at any time, giving you flexibility and allowing you to experiment with different builds for characters and teams.

But regardless of what builds you use, there are some things you’ll need to get a handle on no matter what. Zero Company is a great introduction to the turn-based tactical genre, but it throws a lot at you during its tutorial missions. If you’re new to the genre, it can be tough to remember everything or realize how important some of the basics are.

That’s what we’re here to help with today. These are four things that you can utilize from the opening chapters all the way to the end of the game, and mastering them early can really help your missions run smoothly.

Aggressively attacking on your turn is a big part of combat, but don’t forget about Overwatch. It’s available on every turn to almost every member of your team (notably not the Padawan or Astromech droids). It allows you to create a cone-shaped area on the battlefield, and that character will automatically shoot at an enemy that moves or takes an action in that area.

So when you’re in a situation where every enemy is hiding behind cover and you don’t have enough AP to flank them, Overwatch can come in clutch. It lets you attack enemies during their turn when they run out into the open. But pay attention to the colors of your Overwatch cone as you’re creating it. Blue sections are areas where you’ll shoot at enemies, but grayed out zones are blind spots where cover is blocking your line of sight, meaning you won’t fire a shot at an enemy in that zone.

Overwatch is capable of extending over a significant distance, but the longer you extend, the lower your accuracy will be. You can see your percentage chance to hit as you’re choosing where to place your cone, and it will continually drop by 5% the farther you reach. So you want to find a happy medium, where you’re covering enough space to be confident an enemy will run into that area, but not extending so far that your shots will probably miss.

Overwatch is particularly useful when enemy reinforcements are on the way. You’ll get on-screen prompts letting you know where they’re coming from, so you can set up firing squads and greet the arriving enemies with blaster bolts before they ever have a chance to attack. It’s also important to remember that putting a character into Overwatch will use all of their remaining AP, and the number of enemies they can fire at is equal to how much AP they spent. So you can attack up to three enemies with one character’s Overwatch if you position it well.

The tutorial missions will introduce you to the Call for Backup system, but it might not convey just how pivotal this will be for the whole game. In every turn of combat, a member of your team will get the ability to request backup, where you can choose any teammate to pair up with and attack the same enemy back-to-back.

The character that can request backup is random on each turn, and they’re noted by an icon you can see on their portrait in the bottom left corner of the screen. You should make use of this on every turn, because it’s a free attack that costs no action points. And even better: the backup character’s attack is guaranteed to hit.

The only caveat is that both characters need to have line of sight on the same enemy in order to pull off a combo attack. Once you’ve chosen an ally to back you up, you can double check their status in the top right corner of the screen when you’re lining up the first attacker’s shot. If the backup character doesn’t have line of sight, it will say so. If they do, it will say “Assisting,” meaning they will successfully attack.

There are many strategic uses for these assisted shots. The assisting character will follow up on any attack, not just a regular blaster shot. There are multiple specializations that have extra powerful attacks, and assisted shots will fire after those too. You can use this to pile up a ton of damage at once on exposed enemies, which is especially useful against ones who can counter attack, since you want to finish them quickly. Or since the backup shot is guaranteed to hit, you can use it to finish off an enemy that’s low on health and is trying to hide far away behind cover.

The biggest long-term benefit of backup shots is that they gain bond points for the two characters who team up. In Zero Company, the progression of your characters is defined by their bonds. Bond levels will allow you to choose cross training to give the same benefit to both characters, which is how you’ll add to their stats. If you use backup on every turn, you’ll gain bond levels very quickly, and reaching max bond can unlock build-defining boosts, so you want to get there as early as possible.

Advantage is a resource shared by the whole squad that powers some of your best abilities. Whenever you damage an enemy, whether it’s with a regular shot or a utility item, you gain Advantage. So that means if you hit three enemies with a grenade, you get three Advantage all at once. Your current Advantage is displayed in the bottom left corner of the screen, and it maxes out at 10.

There are upgrades you can purchase in the Den that let you start every battle with some Advantage already banked, which can help you start combat with some momentum, especially if you’re a fan of Cly the Mandalorian. And if you’re in a multi-part story mission, your Advantage points will carry over from one phase to the next.

If you plan things well, it’s very easy to build up Advantage quickly, so you don’t need to be shy about using it. And remember that characters can still use their Advantage abilities even after they’ve used up all their AP for that turn. Different ultimate abilities use a different amount of Advantage, so pay attention to how much each costs so you can use them effectively.

Some abilities that use Advantage, like the Soldier’s Rocket Strike or the Assault’s Sweeping Salvo, are for straightforward damage dealing. Others, like the Medic’s Morale Boost or the Heavy’s Bulwark, are for support or to manipulate the enemy. But they’re all useful in the right hands, and you should use them frequently.

Utilities are items you can equip on characters at the Den. Unlike Advantage, they’re specific to the character they’re equipped on and can’t be shared with teammates. When the game begins, characters will have one utility slot, but you’ll unlock more as you progress.

At the start, most of your utilities will be consumables you can use in combat, like grenades or medpacs. These have limited uses, so you’ll want to pick your spots wisely, but they can swing momentum in a fight when used at the right moment.

As the game goes on, the variety of utility items will increase, giving you access to items that can boost stats and help boost your build. There are items that give you extra defense, increase movement distance, improve your accuracy, increase crit chance, and make you immune to certain status effects. And there are even secondary weapons that unlock unique attacks, like flamethrowers, gas canisters, and scatter guns.

You’ll get utility items as rewards for operations and tactical missions, some of which will be randomized. You can also buy them from the Black Market, which you’ll unlock early in the game, and you can use Den upgrades to increase the odds of getting rare ones. Higher tiers of stat-boosting utility items can give you significant buffs, so don’t ignore them. And don’t forget to equip them either, they don’t do any good just sitting in your inventory.

And there you have it, four tactics that you’ll be able to make use of throughout the whole game. If you’ve been playing Star Wars Zero Company, what have been some of your favorite builds? Let us know in the comments. For more coverage of Zero Company, check out our review and what we wish we knew before starting . And for future entries in The Long Game series, stay tuned to IGN.

articles.title: Miami Approves 'Discreet' GTA 6 Marketing Campaign So the City Can Fix Its Football Field
articles.summary: Rockstar Games' Grand Theft Auto 6 is coming to real-life Miami after a city meeting resulted in the approval of a "discreet" – and controversial – marketing campaign.
articles.body:
Rockstar Games' Grand Theft Auto 6 is coming to real-life Miami after a city meeting resulted in the approval of a "discreet" – and controversial – marketing campaign.

The City of Miami Beach gave the OK for the famed game developer to bring GTA 6 to the area September 10, 2026, following a 4-3 vote in favor of the decision. The meeting saw strong arguments on both sides, with the deal promising that Rockstar will pay at least $3 million to the city as related logos and branding populate the town from October 15 – December 31.

GTA 6's Vice City setting is, of course, based on the very real Miami, Florida , and Rockstar is looking to capitalize on that. Arguments against the move touched on the violence of the Grand Theft Auto series, which, as stated by Commissioner David Suarez, allows players to "steal cars, deal drugs, commit robberies, murder civilians, and assassinate police officers."

"That's their right. They can make it, they can sell it, and they can advertise it, but that doesn't mean that the city of Miami Beach has to help them do it," Suarez argued. "We ask our police officers every day to put themselves in harm's way, protecting this community. We spend enormous resources fighting drugs, violent crime, and disorder, and we've spent over a million dollars over the past three years on a spring break marketing campaign trying to move Miami Beach away from an image of chaos and lawlessness.

"Now, we're going to take our beaches, one of the most recognizable symbols of this city, and turn them into a space for Grand Theft Auto. What kind of message are we sending to the world?"

Later, Suarez added, "I don't think that this is worth what they're offering. I don't think it's worth really anything." Commissioner Matteo-Salinas fell on the other side of the fence. Her vote to approve Rockstar's GTA 6 marketing campaign came from her desire to represent gamers – herself included.

"I play GTA," Matteo-Salinas said. "I played it in 1997 when the first game, the Vice City version, came out, and I'm going to play it again when this one comes out, and I'm not going to play the game and then go on a crime spree. That's not what this is about."

Commissioner Joseph Magazine agreed, arguing that, although "Grand Theft Auto isn't for everyone" and "there are certainly aspects of the game we likely don't want associated with the values" of Miami Beach, "we also have to deal with reality." He added, "I can walk and chew gum at the same time."

"This will be the biggest and most anticipated video game launch in global history, and whether we embrace this partnership or we reject it, millions and millions of people around the world are already going to experience a fictionalized version of Miami Beach through this game. We have no control over that. That spotlight's coming."

Grand Theft Auto 6 vs Real Life Inspiration

How exactly GTA 6 will take over Miami Beach in October was not revealed. However, commissioner Laura Dominguez did tease some of what's on the table.

Rockstar will not plaster logos on city property, such as lifeguard stands or in "iconic public spaces." She said Grand Theft Auto will be advertised "discreetly" with the city's marketing partner, the Boucher Brothers. As mentioned by X/Twitter user @GTAVI_Countdown , the Boucher Brothers is a company Rockstar has parodied before, with its in-game spin instead called "Sol Sisters."

Dominguez added that, through the October – December marketing window, Miami citizens will spot things like "Vice City or 'VI'" on things like chairs and umbrellas. It suggests the words "Grand Theft Auto" won't be visible in any official capacity, with the commissioner also saying that Rockstar will not be permitted to advertise GTA 6 during the city's Art Basel, which is scheduled to take place the weekend of December 4.

"I think the city has done our part to make sure that our brand is protected but still keeping with the importance of the massive global reach that gaming has today, and the city is going to be receiving a couple million dollars," Dominguez said.

She added with a smile, "If there's wiggle room to negotiate more, let us know."

Dominguez mentioned that the deal with Rockstar will give the City of Miami Beach money that is "critical." How exactly the $3 million will be dispersed was not detailed, but Commissioner Tanya K. Bhatt expects the total benefits to produce a number closer to $4 million. She said, "[GTA 6] is coming to Miami Beach with or without us, and to pretend that it isn't is a missed opportunity."

One item on Bhatt's mind when the money comes in is Florida's Flamingo Park. Rockstar's financial support could "in and of itself" pay for a Flamingo Park Memorial Football Field renovation project that is currently slated for next year but lacks proper funding.

"Our city manager and those of us who have engaged have been very clear that this is not to be an in-your-face marketing campaign," she added. "It is very discreet, understated, [and] mostly the Roman numeral six, which most people won't even understand. They'll go around calling it 'V' or 'VI,' probably."

GTA 6's release date falls directly in its Miami Beach marketing window with a November 19, 2026, launch. It will be available for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S. IGN recently got in touch with Rockstar to learn more about how its new take on the series will be worth the wait, resulting in an interview and preview following its big Netflix extended look reveal.

Some fans have recently argued that Rockstar's latest almost looks too realistic for its own good . Others are mostly just concerned with making sure they're able to grab one of the new limited edition PS5 controllers .

This is a true Wi-Fi 7 whole home mesh networking system that includes three satellites (any one of them can be used as the primary router). A mesh system uses satellites that work in tandem with the main router to increase coverage. The more satellites you have, the better the coverage. Three satellites should sufficiently cover most houses.

On the wireless side, this system supports tri-band Wi-Fi 7 with MLO, which means it can work simultaneously across all three bands (2.4GHz, 5GHz, and 6GHz). The BE1000 being a Wi-Fi router can utilize 320MHz channels on the 6GHz band, which is not possible with WiFi 6e. In terms of actual bandwidth performance, TP-Link claims up to 10Gbps, although real world numbers are closer to 2Gbps under ideal circumstances, which is 2X faster than gigabit, the previous gold standard.

On the wired side, each satellite has four 2.5Gbps ethernet ports that support wired backhaul for improved mesh networking performance. If you're one of the lucky ones who is signed up for fiber optic or other ISP provider with higher-than-gigabit internet, then you'll want a router with 2.5Gbps ports to take full advantage of the extra bandwidth. Although there are other routers with 5Gbps or 10Gbps ports, they are prohibitively more expensive

I should also mention that your window to purchase networking products from TP-Link may be closing soon. According to PCMag and other news outlets, the sale of new foreign-made Wi-Fi routers are now banned in the US, including products from TP-Link. This only applies to the sale of new products, not existing ones that are already available on the market. Once this model gets replaced by a newer SKU, you may find it harder to get one here in the States.

articles.title: Magic: The Gathering’s Newest Legendary Artifact Destroys Whole Universes (and Your Creatures)
articles.summary: We've got a first look at two new cards from Reality Fracture.
articles.body:
Magic: The Gathering’s next set is the world-bending Reality Fracture, which centers around an alternate universe with twisted mirror versions of many the game’s characters (available for preorder at Amazon ). We’ve got an exclusive look at two new cards from the set, and while they are a little less twisted than others, they are both pivotal to the story that plays out (so here’s a spoiler warning if you were waiting to read that first).

The first card is a key object in Reality Fracture: The Echoverse Fulcrum. This Mythic Rare legendary artifact is meant to merge universes together, but its functional effect is a board wipe with a little bit of card selection attached.

Colorless cards have had plenty of conditional board wipes like this before, but to my eyes, the low initial mana cost and immediate benefit of drawing and then discarding a card could make this one more broadly useful in a format like Commander. Five mana to activate its ability and only at sorcery speed are both real drawbacks, but that’s easier to stomach when you’ve already gotten something (admittedly minor) out of it.

The other card we are revealing depicts the final moments of Reality Fracture’s hero-turned-villain, Jace. Vraska’s Final Mercy is a Rare sorcery that can either be a removal spell or effectively draw you two cards as it either strikes down or builds up Jace himself.

The first mode’s most immediate parallel is Infernal Grasp , which also destroys a creature at the cost of two life. There are some important differences, though: Vraska’s Final Mercy also hits planeswalkers, but it is severely hampered by being a sorcery instead of an instant, and the mana cost is much more demanding with two black pips.

The second mode’s easiest point of comparison is probably Night’s Whisper , though there are caveats here as well. In addition to the same mana cost difference, the Empower Jace mechanic means you are only able to draw one card the turn you play this and the other on your next turn. It also gives you the flexibility of giving a big boost of loyalty to your Jace token for other shenanigans, and the ability to Surveil if you want to that instead of draw, but not drawing two cards right away is quite rough.

So while it’s arguably worse versions of two similar cards stapled together, it’s not one to fully count out when it comes to stuff like Draft or Sealed, because having options is always powerful in Limited formats like that. My guess is that this card, like The Echoverse Fulcrum, won’t make a ton of waves outside them, but it is an interesting design all the same – and the story moment it depicts makes it quite a flavorful one.

Reality Fracture arrives on MTG Arena on September 29, followed by its tabletop release on October 2, with pre-release events kicking off on September 25. This is the capstone to a story that’s been building for multiple years now, and the last Magic-themed set before it goes back to Universes Beyond with a Star Trek expansion later this year.

Tom Marks is IGN's Associate Reviews Director for games. He loves card games, puzzles, platformers, puzzle-platformers, and lots more.

articles.title: Point Break TV Show Gets the Green Light at AMC
articles.summary: AMC has given its Point Break TV show the green light.
articles.body:
AMC has given its Point Break TV show the green light.

A sequel series based on Keanu Reeves and Patrick Swayze's iconic action movie has officially received a series order from AMC and AMC+, according to Variety . AMC Studios and StudioCanal will co-produce the project, with production on an eight-episode Season 1 set to begin early 2027.

"More than three decades after the events of the original Point Break film, a new heist crew inspired by the Ex-Presidents has emerged and the FBI must rely on a mysterious ex-pro surfer with a checkered past to infiltrate them," an official logline shared by the site said.

Butterfly producer Dave Kalstein and Sugar producer Christopher C. Rogers will lead the new Point Break show as co-showrunners and executive producers. Alcon's Andrew Kosove and Broderick Johnson are executive producers, with Ben Roberts and Julia Cohen also in the mix.

Being set 30 years after the events of the original film, it's unclear if Reeves will play any part in the series. Additional plot information, including who will star in the project, has also not been revealed.

Point Break is a quintessential '90s movie. Originally released back in July 1991, the Kathryn Bigelow-directed film starred Reeves as FBI agent Johnny Utah and Swayze as a bank robber/surfer named Bodhi.

It's a Southern California-set story that has emerged as a cult classic in the decades since its release. Word of a TV adaptation first arrived late last year, with today's news confirming that the show will happen, but the AMC show won't be the first crack at someone else trying to ride its wave.

Alcon released a Point Break remake starring Luke Bracey as Utah and Edgar Ramirez as Bodhi in 2015. It failed to have the sea legs of the film it pulled from, earning lackluster reviews from critics, including a 5/10 from IGN. Our review of the first crack at the IP returned much more favorable results.

"It's fun, and it covers a lot of ground," we said in our 8/10 review . "You really get your money's worth."

articles.title: Polyarc, Dev Behind the Critically Acclaimed Moss Series, Is Shutting Down
articles.summary: Polyarc Games, the developer behind the critically acclaimed Moss games, has announced it is shutting down.
articles.body:
Polyarc Games, the developer behind the critically acclaimed Moss games, has announced it is shutting down.

The Seattle studio announced it is ceasing operations starting today, September 11, 2026, with a post on LinkedIn . It's a shock announcement that will see the company close its doors after 12 years.

"After nearly 12 years riding the joyous rollercoaster of emotions that is making video games, our time together has come to an end," Polyarc said. "As we wind down active development, we are saying our farewells to each other.

"Working together over all of these years has been an honor. Bringing surprise and delight to those who played our games has been a privilege. Thank you to everyone at Polyarc, our work is now finished. Polyarc has been home to exceptional developers across all disciplines.

The post then signed off, encouraging game developers looking for talent to hire members of its team. The full list shared with the message totals 29 names, including artists, designers, animation experts, engineers, and more.

"Thank you to everyone who has been part of this journey," Polyarc signed off.

Polyarc developed and published its first title, Moss VR , in 2018. An action-adventure puzzle game starring a small mouse named Quill, the game was well-received by critics and fans alike. IGN gave it an 8.5/10 upon its release, saying, "Quill and her fantastical world of Moss are instantly likable. This storybook action-adventure makes stellar use of VR."

We also found 2022's Moss: Book 2 to be found similarly enjoyable. In our 8/10 review , we said it "builds upon its predecessor nicely with a captivating world and entertaining platforming, let down primarily by the PSVR’s aging tech."

In 2023, Polyarc released Glassbreakers: Champions of Moss , a more tactical take on the series. A non-VR version of both Moss and its sequel, Moss: The Forgotten Relic , was released just two months ago in July 2026. It also received an 8/10 from IGN .

"Moss: The Forgotten Relic is an incredibly charming fairy tale, and aside from a couple of minor issues, this is a very smooth remake that doesn’t feel compromised by breaking free of its VR-exclusive origins," we said at the time.

Polyarc is, unfortunately, far from the first studio closure in 2026. PlayStation's Bluepoint Games and Dark Outlaw Games were both shut down earlier this year. Ubisoft announced it was closing some of its studios in June. The list goes on, with Netflix also shuttering Oxenfree developer Night School just last month. GreedFall developer Spiders shut down in April. Microsoft announced plans to cut 3,200 staff in July.
